A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SciLitLLM and its CPT/SFT pipeline. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support comparison, including identification of revised experiments and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original base-model evaluations, scientific literature understanding results, and ablation experiments in Tables 2–7. Table 3 distinguishes borrowed baseline results from the authors' experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of its revised model lineup and corresponding ablations in Tables 2–7, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

M1.justification: SciLitLLM's pretrained backbone changes from Qwen2 to Qwen2.5. The substantive procedure remains sequential CPT and SFT with PDF correction, corpus filtering, keyword/task-guided instruction synthesis, deduplication, and instruction filtering. No new pipeline component, objective, or inference mechanism is introduced.

E1.justification: Base-model evaluation replaces MMLU, CMMLU, and English/Chinese Xiezhi STEM subsets with MMLU-Pro biology, chemistry, and health plus MaScQA. SciAssess changes from 29 tasks across five domains to 27 listed tasks across four domains, including new ChartQA rows; this exceeds domain renaming. v3 Appendix D inconsistently says 28 tasks. SciRIFF coverage and the training domains described in Appendix C.1 remain largely unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces the broad ChatGLM, Llama2/3, Qwen1.5/2, Mistral, and Mixtral comparison with Llama3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B/14B. In Table 3, Llama3 and Qwen2 comparators become Llama3.1 and Qwen2.5, with an additional Qwen2.5-14B comparator. SciTulu-7B, Mistral-7B, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4o remain in the instruction-model comparison.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations change from 7B and 72B QLoRA variants to 7B and 14B variants. Section 3.2.3 changes the maximum SFT learning rate from 5e-6 to 1e-5, and the reported SciLitIns training-set size changes from approximately 110,000 to 93,894 instructions. The CPT token budget, training-stage sequence, epoch counts, and sequence lengths are retained. These are reported setting revisions, without independently establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same three ablation questions: CPT's contribution, the SFT data mixture, and instruction filtering. Their evidence is revised for the new model/training configuration, including a positive SFT-only result on both benchmarks and smaller filtering benefits. No new ablation factor or robustness suite is added; appendix examples and quality-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for the model comparisons. Both report point estimates; the retained data-quality histograms do not quantify experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 2–7 extensively replace numerical results. SciLitLLM-7B's reported SciAssess/SciRIFF means change from 52.4/59.4 to 51.7/60.6; new 14B results of 58.2/64.4 replace the 72B results of 59.5/59.7. Changed backbones and SciAssess coverage prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains or losses. v3 Section 4.2.2 claims a 4.6-point SciAssess advantage over its 14B comparator, whereas Table 3 gives 58.2 minus 53.8, or 4.4 points.

T1.justification: v3 removes the explicit autoregressive and supervised fine-tuning objective definitions presented as Equations 1–2 in v1 Sections 2.1–2.2. This is a limited removal of background mathematical formalization. The Levenshtein-based similarity definition in Appendix C.2 remains; neither version provides theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain the combined CPT/SFT pipeline, SciLitIns synthesis, and competitive scientific literature understanding. The performance contribution shifts from a leading 72B QLoRA model to a 14B model claimed to outperform approximately five-times-larger open-source models. v1's introduction claim of successful real-world deployment is removed.

C2.justification: Section 4.3.1 changes from emphasizing weak or absent SFT-only gains to describing benefits from SFT alone plus incremental CPT gains. Section 4.3.2 replaces the explanation of disjoint benchmark domains with a narrower-versus-broader coverage explanation. The new Ethics Statement acknowledges propagation of literature and domain-representation biases; the three principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a SciLitIns dataset access link, updates the model-weight destination to SciLitLLM-1.5, and states that pipeline code accompanies the supplementary material. Appendix D and footnote 8 identify GPT-4o as the MuP/Qasper evaluator; v1 did not specify that evaluator, so this is additional disclosure rather than a demonstrated switch. Training-time information is revised, while appendix recipes mostly remain. Dataset-release statements conflict between the abstract and Reproducibility Statement.

R1.justification: v3 introduces references for Qwen2.5, MMLU-Pro, and MaScQA and removes references associated with discontinued configurations or benchmarks, including QLoRA, LoRA, CMMLU, and Xiezhi. Its substantive positioning against scientific SFT-only and pretraining-only approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses the abstract and several related-work and method passages, revises subsection wording and experimental narration, and adds Ethics and Reproducibility Statements. The main Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–E retain their overall order, and much explanatory prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from an ACM-style two-column layout to a single-column format, with redesigned front matter and extensively resized or repositioned figures, tables, and appendix examples. New Figure 1 visualizes SciRIFF scores against model size. The original instruction-quality Figure 5 moves to the appendix as Figure 7, while Tables 2, 3, and 7 are restructured and the ablation tables are arranged together.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves practical usefulness and transparency through updated model comparisons, explicit SciLitIns access information, and disclosure of the SciRIFF evaluator, while preserving detailed appendix recipes. These benefits are limited: the experiments largely replace existing coverage, including removal of Chinese benchmark evaluations, and uncertainty reporting remains absent. The conflicting release statements, 27-versus-28 task count, and 4.6-versus-4.4-point performance claim weaken the revision's reporting quality and preclude a substantial improvement.
